title: Syracuse restaurant job and Vincent Lopez's offer
summary: His band played a Chinese-American restaurant in Syracuse where Vincent Lopez offered them a hotel job they turned down.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: You asked me what I was doing during the summer, if I can go back. During the -- one of these bands that came to
play a house party, I sat in and what's his name, the guy's in the movies now or was. He was a drummer. A real clown. He's a comedian and he used to do a lot of things, but he was in the band.
Fuzzy Knight. Remember Fuzzy Knight, he used to do some singing there. And later he went out in the movies and did a lot of hillbilly stuff. He was a hillbilly.

But this band, they had a job up in Syracuse in a Chinese-American restaurant. The guy came to me one time and he asked me if I'd like to take that job. He said, 'I think your band could do it well and you might like to do a job like that, the thing is you have to play two hours, and -- two hours from 6 to 8 and then you come back at 9 and play until 12. It's a lot of work, but you could get paid reasonably well.'

So I asked some of the guys and if they wanted to do that, and they said, 'We will stay together during the summer' and this was at the end of my junior year, so I'd still have to go back to Bucknell at the end of the summer.

So we took the job, and we went up there with the band and played and had a good time, got very well acquainted with the Chinese food and it was a lot of writing, you have to keep up with the tunes and the band got, you know, what it's got to get better, with all that playing. It got pretty good.
Well, one night there, who walks in but Vincent Lopez,

and he comes in with the manager or some such thing and listens to the band, likes the band and he says, 'They're going to open up a hotel here. Hotel Syracuse. How would you like the job?' He said, 'All we'll do is open it. I'll be there the first night,' and he said, 'You can have the job.' He said, 'You can go to school up here in Syracuse.'

Well, I guess we were loyal Bucknellians. To a man they wanted to go back home, I guess, and show the band off. So we turned that down, but it was a mark, you know, that a guy like Lopez would come along and liked the band. So we played -- that was one summer that we did stay in the business. And we came back to Bucknell and that was before I had a bass.

Then we had the bass and the band began to sound good and solid with a little bottom in it and we hated to give it up, but we had to do that. So I was out about a month, I didn't know what to do and I figured that --
